title: Affine residue surjectivity splits a map onto a finite-presentation flat module
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $M,N$ be quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, pqf-def-coherent], and let $f:M\to N$ be a module morphism. Assume that $N$ is of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine] and flat over $\mathrm{id}_S$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. For every $s\in S$ let $i_s:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S$ be the residue-field morphism [def-pc-base-change]. If $i_s^*f$ is an epimorphism for every $s$, then $f$ has a right inverse as a morphism of $\mathcal O_S$-modules.

source.place: Tags 068V, 068U, 00NX and 00MT; explicit finite-projective split cancellation argument, expanded by F2

proof.text: Let C be the sheaf cokernel of f. The source isQuasicoherent_cokernel proves that C is quasi-coherent. It is finite type: choose finite local generating data for N (finite presentation implies finite type), and compose each generating epimorphism with the restriction of cokernel.π f. Mathlib GeneratingSections.ofEpi preserves the finite index type. This is the proved private finiteType_of_epi helper, the elementary finite-generating-family argument of Stacks 01B7.

For each x, compare tensorPullback i_x and Mathlib pullback i_x by uniqueness of left adjoints to pushforward (the existing nonempty_tensorPullbackAdjunction and pullbackPushforwardAdjunction). Naturality transports the assumed epimorphism to tensorPullback i_x. This left adjoint preserves the cokernel, so its value on C is zero. Apply finiteType_module_support_pullback to C and i_x. At the closed point y of Spec κ(x), the pullback has zero stalk and i_x(y)=x; the support equality implies that C has zero stalk at x. The module stalk functor sends zero objects to zero objects. Sheaf section separation makes id_C zero, and Abelian.epi_of_cokernel_π_eq_zero gives Epi f. This is the proved private epi_of_residue_epi helper.

Set A=Γ(S,top) and j=(isAffineOpen_top S).fromSpec, an isomorphism because S is affine. Restrict M, N and f along j. Restriction preserves the epimorphism and quasi-coherence. The quasi-coherent fromTildeΓ counits are isomorphisms; their naturality identifies tilde of the section map with the restricted f up to these isomorphisms. Full faithfulness of tilde reflects epimorphisms, so the section map g is epic.

Use the proved source finitePresentation_sections_of_isFinitePresentation to make Γ(N,top) finitely presented. Evaluate IsFlatOver at both top affine opens and rewrite the identity morphism appLE as the identity ring map; this gives flatness with the original section action. Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation proves projectivity. Transport it to the restricted section module through the source sectionsRestrictFromSpecLinearEquiv. Projective.factorThru of the identity along g gives r with r≫g=id.

Conjugate tilde.map r by the inverse target counit and source counit to obtain a right inverse r′ to the restricted f. Counit naturality, functoriality and r≫g=id prove r′≫f′=id. Restrict r′ along inv j and conjugate by the natural isomorphism restrictFunctor j ⋙ restrictFunctor (inv j) ≅ identity, built from restrictFunctorComp, restrictFunctorCongr and restrictFunctorId. Its naturality proves the final right-inverse identity. The proof includes zero modules and the empty affine scheme: no nontrivial section ring is assumed and sheaf separation remains valid with no points.

theorem affine_isSplitEpi_of_residue_epi (S : Scheme.{u}) (hS : IsAffine S)
    (M N : S.Modules) (f : M ⟶ N)
    (hMqc : M.IsQuasicoherent) (hNqc : N.IsQuasicoherent)
    (hNflat : N.IsFlatOver (𝟙 S)) (hNfp : N.IsFinitePresentation)

    IsSplitEpi f
